source: Section 3 of the attribution page (3.1-3.4) and the labels of the static infographic i3-method-map. Run counts restate 3.1 (one run per signal), 3.2 (v(N) and v(N without k)) and 3.4 (2^K coalition values).

rerun.title: Rerun with subsets of signals
rerun.note: needs a policy we can rerun

inside.title: Optimality equations at the joint optimum

methods.title: Stand-alone proxies
methods.text: one signal at a time, own risk target; NNLS fit, residual kept
methods.detail: Reruns the construction with one signal active at a time, each with its own risk target: *K* runs. Fits the total P&L on the *K* proxy P&Ls by nonnegative least squares and keeps the residual.

methods.title: Leave-one-out
methods.detail: Runs the construction with all signals, then once without each signal: *K* + 1 runs.

methods.title: Shapley
methods.detail: Needs the value of every coalition of signals, 2*^{K}* values, and averages each signal's marginal contributions over them.

methods.title: Durin (2014)
methods.text: binding constraints and multipliers give effective matrices *!{Q}_{t}*, *!{P}_{t}*, the same for every signal; *x_{t}* = Σ*_{k}* *x_{t}^{k}*, an exact split
methods.detail: No rerun. Reads the optimal positions, binding constraints and Lagrange multipliers of the joint optimum; the effective matrices are the same for every signal, and the signal positions add up to *x_{t}* exactly.

methods.title: Grinold–Easton
methods.text: each constraint is a separate source: constraint portfolios beside the signal portfolios
methods.detail: No rerun. Keeps each constraint as a separate source: its multiplier's contribution goes through the same recursion and builds a constraint portfolio beside the signal portfolios.
